items.headline: Haze pushes Singapore's air quality back into the unhealthy range
items.summary: The 24-hour PSI in central Singapore climbed back into the unhealthy band over the weekend as smoke from fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan drifted in, prompting the NEA to issue daily advisories.

items.headline: iPhone 18 launch draws overnight queues at Apple's Orchard Road store
items.summary: More than 120 people queued at the Orchard Road Apple store for the iPhone 18 Pro launch on Sep 18; stock ran out before 10am.

items.headline: Six Malaysians jailed over a S$4.9 million machete robbery at a King Albert Park bungalow
items.summary: Six Malaysian men were sentenced after storming a Good Class Bungalow with machetes and robbing poker players of S$4.9 million.

items.headline: Firm fined S$24,000 after its private investigators tailed a police officer
items.summary: A 33-year-old partner of a Singapore investigation firm was fined S$24,000 after its private investigators surveilled a serving police officer.

items.headline: Trump extends the $100,000 H-1B fee, squeezing India's IT giants
items.summary: Trump signed a proclamation on Sep 18 extending the $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions through 2027; Wipro's H-1B approvals fell 62% and TCS's 53% year-on-year.

items.headline: India's economy is rebounding even as US tariffs bite
items.summary: Bloomberg Economics' tracker put India's September growth near 5.2% y/y, up from 4.3% in August, despite Washington's 50% tariffs.

items.headline: Burnham warns of a 'challenging' autumn budget as borrowing costs bite
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham cautioned his Oct 28 budget will be challenging amid rising inflation and borrowing costs, while pledging not to raise income tax, NI or VAT.

items.headline: Ukraine hits Moscow with what officials call its largest drone assault yet
items.summary: Ukraine fired 1,000+ drones at Russia overnight; Moscow's mayor called it the largest such assault, with ~450 downed near the capital, at least two killed and a refinery damaged, as Russia's election closed.

items.headline: United Russia set to keep its grip in a wartime parliamentary vote
items.summary: United Russia was on course to retain its Duma majority, with an exit poll near 49% and no real opposition; Putin framed the vote as a war-support test.

items.headline: Israeli fire kills Palestinians in Gaza, including a health official's son
items.summary: At least three Palestinians, including the son of Gaza's health chief, were killed in Israeli strikes; a child later died near Nuseirat, despite the October ceasefire.

items.headline: Meta launches Muse, a personal AI agent that runs errands for you
items.summary: Meta rolled out Muse, a consumer AI agent that browses, fills forms, emails, books and pays, with free plus $20 and $100 monthly US tiers.

items.headline: Nvidia-backed AI cloud firm Nscale files for a US IPO
items.summary: Nvidia-backed Nscale filed publicly for a US listing, with H1 revenue ~$141M (up 1,200%+), a ~$1B net loss, and a target valuation near $30B.

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5%, its highest since 2023
items.summary: A global bond sell-off on inflation and heavy borrowing pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield to about 5.01% by Sep 18, the first time at 5% since 2023.

items.headline: Gold climbs back toward $4,400 as post-Fed inflation fears ease
items.summary: Gold pushed toward $4,400 an ounce on Sep 18, a weekly high, as easing oil dragged Treasury yields off highs after the Fed's first hike in three years.

items.headline: 🏏 Shafali's 49-ball ton fires India into the Asian Games cricket final
items.summary: Shafali Verma hit 100* off 49 balls (nine sixes) as India beat Bangladesh by 114 runs to reach the Asian Games final; Mandhana became the leading women's T20I run-scorer.

items.headline: 🏏 Australia edge Zimbabwe by one wicket to sweep the ODI series
items.summary: Josh Inglis's century and Nathan Ellis's 36* took Australia to a one-wicket win (272/9 chasing 271) and a 3-0 sweep on their first Zimbabwe tour in 12 years.

items.headline: 🎾 Germany, Canada and Czechia reach the Davis Cup Final 8 as the US falls
items.summary: Zverev sealed Germany, Auger-Aliassime downed France for Canada, and Lehecka's win saw Czechia beat the US 3-2; they join Austria and South Korea in the Bologna finals.

items.headline: 🏎️ Hamilton says 'there's no stopping' Antonelli as the title race tilts
items.summary: Hamilton all but conceded the 2026 title to leader Kimi Antonelli, who is 81 points clear of Russell with Hamilton 101 back; the Azerbaijan GP in Baku is next on Sep 26.

items.headline: Scientists find a hidden 'immune organ' in the skull that helps fight brain cancer
items.summary: Researchers reported immune structures in the skull's bone marrow that defend the brain; in mice a protein gel boosted tumour rejection and survival.

items.headline: Hubble spots a new 10-sided 'decagon' over Saturn's south pole
items.summary: Hubble revealed a giant, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave around Saturn's south pole, a southern cousin to its famous northern hexagon.

items.headline: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS flares up as it heads out of the solar system
items.summary: NASA telescopes report 3I/ATLAS, only the third known interstellar object, brightening and shedding water vapour, CO2 and dust as it exits the solar system.

fun_fact.headline: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun
fun_fact.body: A single bolt of lightning can superheat the surrounding air to roughly 30,000 C (about 54,000 F), nearly five times hotter than the visible surface of the Sun (~5,500 C). The near-instant heating makes the air expand violently, producing the crack of thunder.
fun_fact.source: NOAA National Weather Service; Encyclopaedia Britannica

puzzle.title: Count the Pages
puzzle.body: A book's pages are numbered consecutively from page 1. The printer used exactly 1,392 digits to print all the page numbers. How many pages does the book have?
puzzle.approach: Count the digits used by 1-, 2- and 3-digit page numbers separately, then work backwards.
puzzle.answer: 500 pages. Pages 1-9 use 9 digits; 10-99 use 180; that leaves 1,203 digits for 3-digit pages; 1,203/3 = 401 pages (100-500).

word_puzzle.title: Head of the Class
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange all 12 letters of THE CLASSROOM into a single word: the person who traditionally ran one.
word_puzzle.approach: Every letter is used exactly once.
